The text presents several new examples of difference families constructed on cyclic groups of orders 47 and 97. These combinatorial structures are carefully designed so that their parameters satisfy the conditions required for the construction of skew-Hadamard matrices.

Using the difference families defined on the cyclic group of order 47, the authors construct skew-Hadamard matrices of order 188. Similarly, the difference families constructed on the cyclic group of order 97 lead to skew-Hadamard matrices of order 388. In each case, the order of the resulting matrix is four times the order of the underlying cyclic group, as is typical in constructions based on the Goethals-Seidel array.

A notable feature of these results is their novelty: the difference families described in the text, as well as the corresponding skew-Hadamard matrices obtained from them, are constructed for the first time. Thus, the work contributes new examples to the theory of combinatorial designs and Hadamard matrices.

The skew-Hadamard matrices are obtained by applying the Goethals-Seidel array construction. This method uses suitable supplementary difference sets, or difference families, to build a block matrix whose entries satisfy the Hadamard condition. When the initial difference family has the appropriate skew property, the resulting Hadamard matrix is skew-Hadamard. Therefore, the constructions on the cyclic groups of orders 47 and 97 directly yield new skew-Hadamard matrices of orders 188 and 388, respectively.
outputs.L4:
The text presents a construction of new difference families in cyclic groups of orders 47 and 97 and explains how these combinatorial objects can be used to obtain skew-Hadamard matrices through the Goethals-Seidel array. Difference families are important structures in design theory, and cyclic examples are especially valuable because they often lead to highly symmetric designs and matrices. In this work, suitable base blocks are found in the additive cyclic groups of order 47 and 97, and their difference properties are verified so that they satisfy the required parameters.

Using these difference families as input for the Goethals-Seidel construction, the text then produces skew-Hadamard matrices of orders \(4 \cdot 47 = 188\) and \(4 \cdot 97 = 388\). A skew-Hadamard matrix is a Hadamard matrix with the additional property that, after subtracting the identity matrix, the result is skew-symmetric. Such matrices are of continuing interest in combinatorics, coding theory, and related areas, but explicit constructions are known only for certain orders.

The main contribution reported is the first known construction of difference families with these parameters in the cyclic groups of orders 47 and 97. Consequently, the resulting skew-Hadamard matrices of orders 188 and 388 are also new examples. These constructions extend the catalogue of known skew-Hadamard matrices and demonstrate the usefulness of cyclic difference families together with the Goethals-Seidel array as a method for producing new matrices of this type.

The **Hadamard** matrix is an important object in mathematics, especially in linear algebra, combinatorics, and signal processing. Such matrices are square matrices whose entries are only \(+1\) or \(-1\), and whose rows are mutually orthogonal. **The** special structure of a Hadamard matrix makes it useful in error-correcting codes, experimental design, and digital communications.

Such mathematical objects show how simple patterns can create powerful results. The study of Hadamard matrices continues to be an active area of research, partly because many questions about their existence and construction remain open. In this way, the Hadamard matrix is both a practical tool and a fascinating theoretical concept.

These families satisfy the required parameter conditions for generating supplementary difference sets with skew type structure, and they give rise, via the standard Goethals–Seidel array construction, to skew-Hadamard matrices of orders \(4\cdot 47=188\) and \(4\cdot 97=388\). These results expand the catalogue of known cyclic difference-family constructions and provide new instances of skew-Hadamard matrices in two orders for which explicit constructions are of independent interest.
